text:
I AUDITED ALL NINE DOCS PAGES INSTEAD OF THE TWO I RULED ON, AND THE FAILURE IS NARROWER AND MORE FIXABLE THAN Q7 IMPLIED.

MEASURED -- mentions of the actual story's own words (ghost, warrior, canoe, shot, sick, Egulac, paddling), question-shaped section headers, and explicit worked examples:

  page                        story-words   question-headers   example
  method/one-honest-success        15              0              0
  scala/getting-started             8              0              0
  method/concepts                   1              7              1
  collaborate/index                 1              0              0
  docs/index                        0              0              0     <-- LANDING PAGE
  method/orientation                0              0              1     <-- "Start here"
  method/evidence                   0              0              0
  reference/decisions               0              0              0
  scala/modules                     0              0              0

THE TWO PAGES A FIRST-TIME READER HITS HAVE ZERO GROUNDING. The landing page, then "Start here" to orientation: 1,325 words between them and NOT ONE WORD OF THE STORY. That is exactly the path the owner took, and it is precisely why he finished it knowing nothing.

THE GOOD MATERIAL EXISTS AND IS BURIED ON PAGES THREE AND FOUR.

  method/one-honest-success has FIFTEEN story references -- the most grounded page on the site, and
  a reader only reaches it by choosing "See a tested example" over "Understand the method".
  method/concepts has SEVEN QUESTION-SHAPED HEADERS -- "Which words support the claim?", "Who
  presents the event as true?", "In what order did things happen?" That is the best structural
  device anywhere on the site. It orients a reader in a way no noun-phrase heading can, and it is
  on the third page.

SO THE FIX IS MOSTLY PROMOTION AND REORDERING, NOT NEW WRITING. Pull the grounded material forward. The site already contains what the first two pages need; it is filed behind them.

scout: concretely --
  1. Landing page: the README's own opening sentence, then the twelve-word quotation and the three
     readings. Both already exist; neither needs inventing.
  2. orientation: adopt concepts' question-header device, and answer each question with a line of
     the story rather than a category name.
  3. Consider whether "Understand the method" and "See a tested example" should be one page. The
     tested example is where the understanding actually is.

AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN INSTRUMENT, because I nearly reported the wrong page as worst. My first pass counted BLOCKQUOTES as the concreteness proxy and ranked method/concepts bottom -- 568 words, no blockquote, no code, no table. Reading it showed an inline example ("the claim 'the warriors said he was shot' belongs to the warriors' speech") and seven question-headers that my grep could not see. CONCRETENESS IS NOT MARKDOWN SYNTAX. I fixed the measure and the ranking changed materially: concepts is one of the better pages, and the landing page is one of the worst.

That is the third measuring instrument I have had to correct today -- the sweep grep that could not see generic types, the blocker loop that could not tell a failed command from an empty list, and now this. Each time the instrument was silent about what it could not see, and each time I nearly published its silence as a finding.
